sampling_model.design: Known independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment on a fixed partition into unequal disjoint cliques.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units, partition, graph, exposure map, and all exposure-indexed potential outcomes are fixed.
sampling_model.treatment: Within block \(l\), All Treat and All Control are mutually exclusive events, each with probability \(q_l=2^{-r_l}\); blocks are independent.
sampling_model.overlap: Every target exposure has known positive probability \(q_l\), which may vary with \(l\) and vanish along triangular arrays.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No superpopulation nuisance is estimated; on a unanimous block, the observed block mean equals the corresponding fixed-schedule block mean, and omitted blocks receive deterministic bias protection.
sampling_model.randomness: The only inferential randomness is \(Z\), augmented by independent \(R\) solely to include externally randomized interval procedures in the decision class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Exposure-weighted estimators are unbiased, conservative randomization variances are available, and local-dependence conditions justify asymptotic normal intervals.

Section 4.3 constructs finite-sample Hoeffding-type confidence intervals for population-average direct, indirect, total, and overall effects of binary outcomes under a two-stage partial-interference design.

Exact confidence sets for binary direct, indirect, total, and overall effects under two-stage randomization and stratified partial interference are obtained by inversion of randomization tests, with a targeted approximation algorithm.
Full-neighborhood exposure probabilities can be exponentially small in degree and graph-cluster randomization can sharply reduce Horvitz--Thompson variance.
Conflict-graph connectivity controls upper and lower minimax mean-squared-error rates when the design and estimator are decision variables.
Under ordinary randomized experiments, nonasymptotic treatment-effect intervals attain the effective sample size \(n\pi\), with matching estimation-rate lower bounds.
Between-class moduli lower-bound expected confidence-interval length and ordered moduli yield procedures within constant factors in Gaussian models.
Convex regression classes admit finite-sample modulus-based optimal intervals and sharp efficiency bounds under normal errors with known variance.
Under interference, existence of unbiased estimators does not guarantee variance that decreases with population size.
Randomized fuzzy intervals attain a minimum expected-length benchmark for a one-parameter Bernoulli observation problem.

body.tldr: Unequal clique sizes turn full-neighborhood All Treat and All Control exposure into independent nonidentical categorical reveals. The exact centered block Horvitz--Thompson increment is at most \(w_l/(2q_l)\), giving the clipped half-width \(\sqrt{S\log(2/\alpha)}+M\log(2/\alpha)/6\). Trimming is within a factor \(5/2\) of the capped water-filling modulus and yields the unrestricted upper bound \(\mathcal R_\alpha\le5\min\{1,\omega_\alpha\}\). A cubic common-location lower bound proves the exact fixed-confidence consistency boundary, and a separate product-Rademacher argument gives \(\Theta_\alpha(k^{-1/2})\) for the stated two-scale family. The sole unresolved sharp-frontier step is a universal linear weighted-erasure lower bound for all measurable externally randomized intervals. The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) diagnostic reports structural graph rejection separately from package-versus-reference exposure-label mismatch and releases the corrected interval only after both checks pass.

project_justification.gap: Existing partial-interference confidence procedures do not characterize worst-case expected length over every measurable externally randomized interval under fixed balanced Bernoulli assignment on unequal cliques. The exact consistency boundary is settled, the capped optimizer and trimming dual are certified, and the unrestricted upper bound is explicit. The sole remaining sharp-frontier gap is to strengthen the proved cubic capped-erasure converse to a universal linear lower bound.
project_justification.niche: The paper treats the known assignment distribution as the sole inferential randomness and exposes three computable design scales: the quadratic rare-exposure scale \(S\), the largest centered-increment scale \(M/2\), and the capped water-filling or trimming scale. The capped scale is necessary and sufficient for fixed-confidence consistency and controls honest length from above even when a dominant rare block makes \(S\) misleading.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution consists of the exact independent categorical block reduction, the observed-data block Horvitz--Thompson estimator, the clipped Bernstein interval with linear term \(M\log(2/\alpha)/6\), the bias-protected trimmed interval, the certified capped water-filling optimizer, the factor-\(5/2\) trimming dual, the factor-five unrestricted upper bound, the cubic all-procedure lower bound, and the exact consistency equivalence. A dedicated product-Rademacher anti-concentration argument also proves the fixed-confidence \(\Theta_\alpha(k^{-1/2})\) rate for the specified two-scale family. The note leaves the universal linear converse open rather than promoting the special-family lower bound to the full class.

body.related_work: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, constructs Hoeffding intervals for binary allocation-strategy effects under two-stage Type-A partial interference, and RigdonHudgens2015 constructs exact confidence sets for those binary two-stage effects. Neither treats this unequal-clique Bernoulli All Treat versus All Control minimax expected-length problem or proves the open water-filling lower frontier. AronowSamii2017 supplies the design--exposure--estimand architecture and exposure-specific inverse weighting, while UganderKarrerBackstromKleinberg2013 shows that full-neighborhood exposure probabilities may be exponentially small in degree. BasseAiroldi2018 gives a nonconcentration warning, UganderYin2023 changes the design to mitigate small exposure probabilities, and KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies design-based mean-squared-error criteria rather than all-interval confidence length. CaiLow2004 and ArmstrongKolesar2018 motivate modulus arguments in Gaussian experiments, but do not provide the heterogeneous weighted-erasure interval-spread theorem required here. The common-location construction is used only for the proved cubic consistency lower bound, and the product-Rademacher argument is confined to the specified two-scale family.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The common-location no-reveal construction yields \(\mathcal R_\alpha\gtrsim\omega_\alpha^3/\log(1/\alpha)\), which is sufficient for the fixed-confidence consistency equivalence but can be much smaller than \(\omega_\alpha\). The unrestricted sharp lower bound and the no-dominance sharp lower half therefore remain open forms of the same universal linear weighted-erasure interval-spread problem. A resolution must control compact-support boundaries, random weighted reveal information, conditional target fluctuation, and external interval randomization; neither the exact embedding, the cubic argument, nor the family-specific product-Rademacher lemma supplies that universal step.
body.honest_scope: The proved results concern fixed outcomes in \([-1/2,1/2]\), known unequal disjoint clique blocks, and independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment. The estimator and upper intervals are measurable from \(D\) and known design quantities. The capped optimizer, factor-\(5/2\) trimming comparison, factor-five unrestricted upper bound, exact consistency boundary, and cubic lower bound cover arbitrary independent external interval randomization. The fixed-confidence \(\Theta_\alpha(k^{-1/2})\) statement is confined to the specified two-scale family; it is not a universal posterior-spread theorem. The equal-block and general no-dominance results retain only their proved upper conclusions. Overlapping or nonclique neighborhoods are rejected before the software diagnostic reports an interval.
body.interpretation: The computable quantity \(\rho_0(w,q)\), equivalently the unit-budget capped modulus \(\omega_1(w,q)\), is the intrinsic consistency diagnostic. A rare block may keep \(S\) bounded away from zero while carrying so little causal weight that trimming it still permits vanishing honest length. At nonzero finite confidence, the corrected trimmed interval has risk at most five times the capped modulus, while the general converse is presently cubic. The sharper \(k^{-1/2}\) lower rate is proved only for the explicit two-scale family and does not settle the universal linear frontier.
